title: Choose the visual world for skills.garciabaertsch.com
question: The roll assigned the Library Card Catalog. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Library Card Catalog
options.lineage: Library of Congress catalog cards and the oak and steel drawers that hold them
options.thesis: The collection is a catalog drawer: every skill is a typed card with an author line and a call number (planning:grill-me), and the suggester is the library's 'see also' card.
materials: white card stock with a red header rule
options.viewport: The drawer front owns the top: a brass label holder reads CLAUDE SKILLS. Below it the first cards stand in the drawer, read top-down: the title card (what this is, one line), the install card with three typed commands and a stamped COPY, and a 'see also' card showing a real suggester exchange.
options.risk: Turns back into a card grid if the cards are laid out as tiles instead of a filed, top-down drawer.

raised.raise: One pull files everything: the install card is the single action, and it visibly files every plugin card at once.
Absence is designed: opt-in plugins (ponytail, observer) stand in the drawer as unfiled cards, present but set apart.
No card without its maker: every skill card carries a ruled author line, linked to the original repository.
It teaches in order: three numbered guide cards walk a newcomer from install to first skill.

options.label: Transit Map
options.thesis: Workflows are lines and skills are stations (grill-me, to-spec, to-tickets, implement); the suggester is the 'change here for' sign.
options.viewport: A diagram where each plugin is a coloured line and the main workflow runs straight across the first screen.
options.risk: Familiar: the subway diagram is a well-worn metaphor for developer tooling.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine Explainer
options.lineage: technical zines sketched like a friend's napkin drawing
options.thesis: Claude Code explained like a friend sketching it: marker lettering, doodled arrows from prompt to skill.
options.viewport: A doodled panel showing a prompt, an arrow, and the skill that answers it.
options.case: Wins on how friendly it feels to beginners, but loses on clarity and conflicts with the neutral voice you chose.
options.risk: Reads playful and unserious next to install commands.

options.label: Miura-fold Sheet
options.case: Abstract: nobody visiting recognises their task in it.
options.kept: One action deploys the whole set.

options.label: Seven-segment Display
options.case: Gimmick: nothing here is a number that changes.
options.kept: Unlit states designed as carefully as lit ones.

options.label: Sapeur Portrait Plate
options.case: No link to skills or Claude Code.
options.kept: Every item named in a ruled caption.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.case: Charming but vague about what the product is.
options.kept: One type voice used with strict discipline.
